features.title: Workspace layout and identity
features.summary: The Workspace as a self-contained, file-native directory selected explicitly by the CLI: where it may live, what it works without, how canonical resources are split into separately persisted units, and how each resource is identified.

rules.statement: A Workspace is the directory that a CLI command selects explicitly (see the Command-line interface Contract), and UIUX owns a fixed internal layout beneath that root.
A Workspace works without a production source tree, Git or network access.
Without Git, UIUX never invents Git revision information; with Git, Handoff may preserve its commit provenance.
Installing `@deviltea/uiux` in the production repository is not required; the runtime is selected by the explicit Workspace path.

Views, UX Flows, Review threads, Locales and authored Assets are separate canonical resources, each persisted as its own unit; the Workspace persisted format Contract gives their paths and the View shape.
Grouping is a logical projection, never a storage layout: no grouping places, nests or moves a View file, and one View can serve any number of groupings and UX Flows without being duplicated.

Views, UX Flows, Review threads and authored Assets each have an immutable full UUID identity stored in the resource, and every reference to them uses that full UUID, never a file path, filename, display name, slug or shortened ID.
A Locale is identified by its canonical BCP 47 tag.

A resource whose stored identity differs from the UUID in its file or directory name, a duplicated identity, and a create that would overwrite an existing resource path all fail explicitly; copying a resource file never creates a new identity.
Display names and other human-readable labels can change without changing a resource's identity.
A Workspace root may sit in a specification repository, a product repository or any ordinary directory; it need not be a Git repository root and is not coupled to a production repository.

features.title: Workspace schema versioning and migration
features.summary: How the single Workspace schema version is recognized, how a Workspace at an older or unsupported version is treated, and the explicit, CLI-only migration that upgrades it.

rules.statement: A Workspace at a recognized older `schemaVersion` can be opened, inspected and explained, but UIUX never mutates or upgrades it implicitly.
A Workspace whose `schemaVersion` is unknown or newer than this UIUX supports is `unsupported` and is reported with one clear schema diagnostic.

Until an older Workspace is migrated, and while a Workspace is `unsupported`, every mutation, formal capture, Handoff readiness assessment and Handoff export is refused with the schema diagnostic that the Workspace persisted format Contract assigns.
Migration runs only when an operator invokes `uiux migrate`; there is no MCP Tool and no HTTP route for it.
While migration is required, the Workbench shows a read-only banner that names the `uiux migrate` command.
Migration upgrades the Workspace in place, deterministically and atomically, to the current `schemaVersion`; a failure leaves the Workspace unchanged, never partially migrated.
One run chains every migration step from the Workspace's version to the current one, in version order; the Workspace persisted format Contract names the steps.
Before anything is written, each step re-validates every Review file that was valid under its source version against its target version.
The step from version 1 to 2 sets `schemaVersion` to 2 and adds `resolution: "verified"` to every Review lifecycle event that entered `resolved` without a resolution.
The step from version 2 to 3 changes only the manifest `schemaVersion`, from 2 to 3.
A dry run, `uiux migrate --dry-run`, plans the migration in memory and writes nothing.
A real migration refuses while a `uiux dev` server is serving the Workspace; a dry run still runs then and notes the serving server.

A release that raises the current `schemaVersion` ships the matching migration step, its validators and the `uiux migrate` entrypoint together, so no released version decodes a new schema without handling it.
The step from version 1 to 2 synthesizes no Review pin display hints.

features.title: Domain mutations and revision concurrency
features.summary: How canonical resources change: only through domain-specific atomic mutations under revision concurrency, shared by every transport through one application layer, with out-of-band edits detected and a retryable refusal when persistence is busy.

rules.statement: Canonical resources change only through domain-specific mutations, each atomic within one resource or domain boundary; a mutation may carry several structured operations against that boundary. There is no generic file write, arbitrary filesystem write or cross-domain Workspace-wide patch.

`/api/*`, `/mcp` and `/preview/*` are separate transport adapters over one shared application and domain layer: MCP never calls `/api/*` over loopback HTTP, and transport routes never duplicate domain logic.
Edits made to canonical files outside UIUX are detected through revisions and validation; such edits bypass mutation-only affordances such as reference-impact acknowledgement.
When the persistence lock cannot be acquired within its wait budget, the operation changes nothing and fails retryably with the busy refusal of the mutation-semantics Contract.

features.title: Reference integrity and destructive changes
features.summary: How destructive or identity-changing operations treat references to their target: reporting the impact and requiring acknowledgement, staying target-local, and keeping dangling or invalid references as repairable diagnostics.

rules.statement: Before deleting a View, UX Flow or authored Asset, renaming a Variant, or renaming a viewport or theme key, the normal Workbench or MCP operation reports the known affected canonical references and proceeds only after the caller explicitly acknowledges that impact.
Such a change stays atomic within its own resource or domain boundary: UIUX never cascades it, auto-rebinds references or silently rewrites referencing resources.

A reference whose target is gone keeps its original target identity and is reported as a structured invalid or dangling diagnostic until it is explicitly repaired; a Workspace with dangling references is a supported, repairable state.

UIUX preserves invalid authored data for repair and reports it; it never silently drops or rewrites it, and never rebinds a reference heuristically by name, type, selector, tree position, geometry or similarity.

features.title: View structure and RootShell
features.summary: The View as one canonical resource: its single Widget IR rooted at the UIUX-managed RootShell, the boundary between UIUX and Adapter-owned Widget semantics, the render context it receives, and its optional display-grouping `feature` tag.

rules.statement: A View owns exactly one canonical Widget IR. Its Variants are initial Runtime State presets over that IR, not alternate Widget trees, snapshots or source patches.

Every View IR is rooted at the UIUX-owned RootShell Widget plugin. UIUX creates it together with the View, ordinary Widget identity allocation never uses its reserved ID, and no other Widget in the tree may be a RootShell.
Authors cannot add Slots to RootShell; adding a system Slot requires a Workspace schema migration.

RootShell presence, type, ID and Slot structure are system-managed: authors may change only RootShell fields that the schema marks user-editable, and deleting, retyping or re-identifying the root or breaking its Slot is invalid, even through a raw file edit.

The Workbench or Preview controller selects the render context: the Variant and, independently of it, the Locale, theme and viewport. RootShell exposes the effective values to descendant Widgets as read-only presentation context; neither descendant Widgets nor Variants can write it.

View IR and Variant state may set only Widget State members that the plugin schema marks author-writable; computed, read-only or internal State stays non-writable, and a write outside that boundary is a validation error.

Beyond the reserved RootShell boundary, the Adapters' Widget plugin definitions own the executable IR semantics (types, schemas, defaults, Slots and Properties); UIUX keeps no second runtime schema for them.
View IR describes view structure, component identity, states, copy and interaction rules; it never carries arbitrary business logic, networking or routing.
A View's optional `feature` tag is used only to group Views for display: untagged Views appear ungrouped, a View belongs to at most one group, and groups are derived from the current Views.
UIUX keeps no Feature entity for that grouping: no persisted Feature object or ID, Feature directory or Feature lifecycle, and no link from the tag to an external Feature or scenario system.
The `feature` tag is not part of Review anchor or UX Flow identity; renaming or changing a group means changing the matching Views' tags, never migrating an identity or moving files.

features.title: View Variants
features.summary: Named Variants of a View: sparse presets of initial Widget Runtime State, their name-based identity, and how invalid Variants are kept and reported.

rules.statement: A named Variant is a sparse preset of initial Widget Runtime State: it stores only the State members it overrides, and every Widget or member it omits keeps the IR and plugin defaults.
Rendering a View without a Variant uses its canonical base state: the IR plus plugin defaults, with no preset applied.
Selecting, switching or capturing a Variant builds a fresh Runtime from the View IR with that Variant's overrides; it never inherits interaction state from an earlier Runtime.
A Variant's name is its stable View-local identity: other resources reference a Variant by its View UUID plus Variant name, and there is no secondary Variant ID or registry.
Renaming a Variant is an explicit identity change that requires updating the references to it.

An invalid Variant (an unknown Widget ID, an unknown or non-author-writable State member, or an invalid value) keeps its authored data for repair, and until it is valid it cannot be used, even partially, for render, capture or formal Review Evidence.
UIUX reports all determinable diagnostics of an invalid Variant together, inline and in Checks.

features.title: Structured View Spec
features.summary: The structured Spec each View carries beside its IR: explicit empty values, and how it references other Views and external material.

rules.statement: A View's Spec is a structured specification kept in the same View file as its IR and Variants but conceptually distinct from the executable IR; the Workspace persisted format Contract lists its fields.
Empty Spec content is stated explicitly, never by omitting a field; whether a Spec is complete is judged by Checks and Review policy, not by which fields are present.
A View reference records a design relationship to a View, optionally to one of its Variants; it never becomes a UX Flow edge or a runtime route.

An external reference is identified by its URI alone: UIUX defines no provider-specific source or ID semantics, no other field of the reference is part of its identity, and its label is non-authoritative display text.
UIUX does not fetch, mirror, synchronize or domain-validate the content behind an external reference, and an unreachable URI never rewrites the Spec.

contracts.title: Workspace persisted format
contracts.summary: The persisted format of a UIUX Workspace, versioned as a whole by the manifest `schemaVersion`: the manifest, the path, file unit and identity of every canonical resource kind and of the content-addressed derived-artifact store, the canonical JSON shapes of those resources, and the diagnostics of a Workspace whose schema is older or unsupported.

clauses.statement: The Workspace manifest is `.uiux/workspace.json` under the Workspace root. The `.uiux/` directory is reserved for UIUX system metadata, such as the manifest and the derived-artifact store.

The manifest is a JSON object holding the Workspace-level settings: `schemaVersion`, `i18n`, the ordered `adapters` list and the `viewports` and `themes` registries. All five are required; an empty `adapters` list or registry is valid.

`schemaVersion` is a positive integer and the only schema version in a Workspace: resource files carry none and are all decoded under it. The current version is 3; versions 1 and 2 are recognized older versions.
The migration steps are `uiux.v1-to-v2`, from `schemaVersion` 1 to 2, and `uiux.v2-to-v3`, from 2 to 3.
A field introduced by a later schema version is invalid (`schema.unknown_field`) in a Workspace at an earlier version; no version treats a later version's field as an optional addition.

An operation refused because the Workspace needs migration reports `workspace.migration_required`, and one refused because its schema is `unsupported` reports `workspace.schema_unsupported`. Over HTTP, formal capture, Handoff readiness assessment and Handoff export refused with `workspace.migration_required` answer 422.

`i18n` is an object whose required `defaultLocale` is a canonical BCP 47 tag. Supported Locales are discovered from Locale files and not listed in the manifest, and `i18n` gains further settings only additively, through schema evolution.

`adapters` is an ordered array whose order is the canonical installation order. Each entry holds a portable module reference (a bare package or module specifier, or a `./` specifier relative to the Workspace root; never an absolute or resolved path) and an optional JSON-compatible Adapter `config`.

`viewports` maps viewport IDs to presets. A viewport ID is a non-empty, case-sensitive, opaque Workspace-local string, and each preset records the exact CSS viewport width and height; labels and other metadata are separate from identity.
`themes` maps theme IDs, which are non-empty, case-sensitive, opaque Workspace-local strings, to theme entries; Adapters validate or map those IDs but do not own them.
Each View is one file `views/<uuid>.view.json`, where `<uuid>` is the View's full UUID and equals its `id`.

A View's top level has exactly `id` (its full UUID), `name` (its required display name), an optional single-valued `feature` tag, `ir`, `variants` and `spec`; derived timestamps, file paths or filenames and a generic `metadata` object are not canonical fields.
`ir` is the RootShell Widget, with type `RootShell`, ID `root` and one Slot, `content`: an ordered array of child Widget sources whose own shape the Adapters' Widget plugins define.

`variants` is an object keyed by Variant name, a non-empty string. Each entry is `{ state }`, where `state` maps Widget IDs to sparse maps of State member overrides (`variants.<name>.state.<widgetId>.<member>`); entries carry no UUID and do not repeat the name, and the entry object stays open to additive metadata.

`spec` always contains `intent` (a string), `entryConditions`, `interactionRules`, `constraints` and `accessibility` (string lists whose items carry no IDs), `references` (typed references) and `decisions` (Decisions).

Each `references` entry is a typed reference discriminated by `type`: `{ type: "view", viewId, variantName?, relation? }` with a full View UUID as `viewId`, or `{ type: "external", uri, label?, relation? }` with a non-empty absolute URI of any scheme as `uri`. An optional `relation` is a non-empty string, and other `type` values are invalid until a schema version adds them.
Each UX Flow is one file `flows/<uuid>.flow.json`, where `<uuid>` equals the Flow's `id`.
Each Review thread is one file `reviews/<uuid>.review.json`, where `<uuid>` equals the thread's `id`.

Each Locale is one file `i18n/<locale>.json`, named by its canonical BCP 47 tag, holding one flat JSON object that maps literal message keys to string values: `.` in a key has no nesting or namespace meaning, and there are no per-View, split or merged Locale files.
Locale files are discovered from `i18n/*.json`; a file whose name is not a canonical BCP 47 tag is diagnosed and excluded from the discovered Locales, never aliased to or merged with another file.
Each authored Asset is one directory `assets/<uuid>/` containing `asset.json` and exactly one source-content file; the directory UUID equals the `id` in `asset.json`.
`asset.json` records at least the Asset `id`, a required display `name`, the source-content filename and the declared `mediaType`; references never depend on display, original or content filenames.
View data binds an Asset only as `{ "$asset": "<assetId>" }`, and only in Adapter Catalog fields declared asset-capable.
Authored Assets under `assets/` are source data; UIUX-generated derived artifacts live separately under `.uiux/artifacts/`.
A derived artifact is identified by `sha256:<hex>` over its bytes and stored immutably under `.uiux/artifacts/sha256/`: identical bytes deduplicate, and an existing blob is never overwritten.

Formal Evidence records are themselves immutable artifacts in that store; there is no mutable `evidence/` resource namespace, and rerunning Evidence creates a new artifact rather than overwriting one.

contracts.title: Command-line interface
contracts.summary: The `uiux` command surface that users and CI depend on: installation as `@deviltea/uiux`, help and version output, and the `init`, `dev`, `migrate`, `publish` and access-administration (`member`, `token`, `invite`, `session`, `access copy`) commands with their arguments, effects and exit status.

clauses.statement: UIUX is installed as the single public npm package `@deviltea/uiux` (`npm install -D @deviltea/uiux`) and invoked through its `uiux` binary, for example `npx uiux init`.
`uiux --help` prints usage and `uiux --version` prints the package version. Help lists a command only once it ships and never advertises an unshipped one.
Every command that acts on a Workspace takes it explicitly as `--workspace <dir>`; UIUX never infers a Workspace from the working directory.

`uiux init --workspace <dir>` creates a minimal valid Workspace: a `.uiux/workspace.json` manifest at the current `schemaVersion` with a `defaultLocale`, no Adapters and empty viewport and theme registries.
`uiux init` refuses a directory whose manifest already exists and leaves it unchanged; it creates the Workspace directory when it does not exist yet.
`uiux dev --workspace <dir>` starts one unified packaged Nitro server for that Workspace, hosting the Workbench SPA, `/api/*`, `/mcp` and `/preview/*`.
Without the opt-in LAN listener, `uiux dev` listens on loopback only and refuses a non-loopback bind host.
`uiux migrate --workspace <dir> [--dry-run]` prints the step IDs, the `schemaVersion` change and the changed files, and a real run also prints the new manifest revision.
`uiux publish --workspace <dir> --out <dir> [--base <path>] [--source-revision <rev>]` builds the read-only static publication of the Workspace into the `--out` directory.

`uiux member`, `uiux token`, `uiux invite`, `uiux session` and `uiux access copy` act only on the host-local roster of the Workspace named by `--workspace`, and refuse a directory that is not an initialized Workspace, so a typo never creates a stray roster.
Rosters live under `$UIUX_HOME` (default `~/.uiux`); `uiux dev` and every access command refuse when `$UIUX_HOME` resolves inside the selected Workspace.

`uiux member add <nick> --role <owner|editor|reviewer|viewer> [--kind human|agent]`, `uiux member list`, `uiux member set <nick> [--role <role>] [--nickname <new>]` and `uiux member remove <nick>` manage the roster's members.

`uiux token create --member <nick> [--label <text>] [--expires <days>|never] [--lan]` prints the new Token; `uiux token list [--member <nick>] [--all]` lists Tokens, with `--all` including revoked and expired ones; `uiux token revoke <token-id>` revokes one.
`uiux invite create --member <nick> [--origin <url>] [--expires <hours>]` prints a single-use sign-in link for a human member.
`uiux session list` lists browser sessions, and `uiux session revoke <session-id>` or `uiux session revoke --member <nick>` ends them.

`uiux access copy --from <old-dir> [--replace]` copies the members and Token hashes of `<old-dir>`'s roster into the selected Workspace's roster once; the target must have no roster unless `--replace` is given.

Exit status is 0 on success (including a migration with nothing to migrate), 1 when a command is refused or fails, and 2 for invalid usage (an unknown command or option, which also prints usage, or missing or extra arguments) or an unusable Workspace root or access home; `uiux dev` exits with its server's status, 0 after SIGINT or SIGTERM.

`uiux dev --lan` also starts the LAN listener, configured by `--lan-address <ip>` (default `0.0.0.0`), `--lan-port <n>` (default: the loopback port + 1), the repeatable `--lan-hostname <name>`, and `--lan-tls-cert <file>` with `--lan-tls-key <file>`, which must be given together; `HOST` and `NITRO_HOST` keep naming only the loopback bind.
